decisions.reason: Uses ls-remote-tags.txt (listing jumps v0.9.1 to v0.9.7, so v0.9.5 is absent) and sync-script.sh (only pushes HEAD:main per mirror, never tags) to explain the README-pinned tag failing resolution as a maintainer tag-distribution defect, explicitly ruling out consumer network or command problems.

Uses dsh-version.txt (0.1.1-rc.2) and compat-table.md to explain that v0.9.7 targets the newer 0.1.2-alpha.1 client API whose useConversation seat does not exist on the older runtime; notes the successful install and restart do not establish API compatibility rather than just repeating the error.

Selects v0.9.3 with the rc.1 verification plus additive rc.2 note, but asserts 'v0.9.3 exists on the mirror' — contradicted by the sealed ls-remote-tags.txt where v0.9.3 is also absent — and presents the unconditional #v0.9.3 install command as immediately workable, with no tag-publication precondition or verified-commit alternative. The central trap of the remedy is missed and contradicted.

Grounded in the branch-only sync script, proposes pushing tags to every mirror (git push <remote> --tags or --follow-tags alongside the branch push) and a post-release git ls-remote --tags verification per mirror that fails the release when the documented tag is missing.

Replaces the single newest-tag default with a README routing matrix (0.1.1-rc.x to v0.9.3, 0.1.2-alpha.1 to v0.9.7) plus a manifest peer constraint for install-time rejection — the core requirement is met, but the '0.1.2-alpha.1+' table row generalizes v0.9.7 support to untested later releases, which the criterion forbids.
